risks: Stale-cycle unwind: `resolve_stale_cycle` aborts a `sending` cycle (hold released) when `resolve_intent_by_hash` returns Ok(None). That is safe only because STALE_CYCLE_SQL selects rows older than RESERVE_REPLENISH_STALE_SECS (600 s, const-asserted >= 2 × the signer's 300 s envelope validity) and the resolver treats NotFound as absent only on a fresh Horizon head — attack the assumption that the prepared envelope's timeout is really 300 s (signer TX_TIMEOUT_SECS) and that Ok(None) for a found-but-failed tx is definitive.

`record_cycle_hash` is a NULL-CAS: a `sending` cycle that already carries a hash can never be re-armed, so a definitively rejected replenishment spend is aborted (`failed`, hold released) rather than retried with a new sequence — intended (mirrors 'never resubmit'), but a reviewer should confirm no path expected a retry from `sending`.

`spend_disposition` freezes an Ambiguous classification even when `!hash_armed` (nothing was submitted). Only a non-BadRequest/non-Retryable prepare error (bad seed) reaches it; freezing for a human there is deliberate but conservative.

`record_spend_sent` now refuses to overwrite a DIFFERENT armed hash: if any pre-037 `sending` row somehow carried a foreign hash it would log 'NOT RECORDABLE' instead of settling. Pre-037 binaries wrote send_tx_hash only at `sent`, so this should be unreachable.

DB-lane `harness::sql_const` depends on the `pub(crate) const NAME: &str = "..."` literal shape with `\`-newline continuations; a constant rebuilt with format!/concat! would panic the extractor loudly (test failure, not silent drift).
